title: Keynesian Economics
text: Keynesian economics, founded by British economist John Maynard Keynes in his 1936 work The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money, argues that aggregate demand — total spending in the economy — is the primary driver of economic output and employment. Keynes challenged classical economics by arguing that wages and prices are sticky downward and that markets do not automatically clear, meaning economies can get stuck in prolonged recessions. He advocated for government fiscal stimulus (deficit spending) to boost demand during downturns. Keynesian ideas were influential in shaping the New Deal and post-World War II economic policies. Neo-Keynesian and New Keynesian economics incorporate Keynesian insights into modern macroeconomic models.
